diagnosis: Writes the sum of each column side by side instead of regrouping ten ones into one ten.
rationale: The student added 3 + 2 = 5 and 7 + 6 = 13, writing 513 side by side. Demonstrating how a group of ones greater than nine bundles into one ten will help them see that ones must be regrouped rather than written as a two-digit number in the ones place.

script.focus: ten ones bundle into one ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [15]. Tutor points at: ten ones bundle into one ten

frames.caption: Here are 15 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 5 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place: 15. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they wrote the two-digit sum (13) directly into the ones place. The chosen demonstration directly isolates why a place value column cannot hold more than 9 and shows bundling 10 ones into 1 ten, perfectly addressing the prerequisite misconception without giving away the exact answer to 37 + 26.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this cleanly demonstrates the core concept of bundling 10 ones into 1 ten to explain why 13 cannot be written in the ones column.
